nodes.end_condition: All four decisions recorded and every implementation node has a write-set that does not overlap another node in the same wave.

nodes.name: F1: Durable sim solve-state cache (.step+ studies + SPICE/EM/CFD result cache)

inputs.request: Implement the RESERVED contracts/stepplus.md studies/*/results.npz seam in the C++ stepplus path so FEA static/modal/thermal solve state (assembled/factored system + result field) persists and reloads, mirroring the geometry cache (engine-key + content-hash keyed, erase-first on save, validate-on-open, honest miss). Add a keyed result cache for SPICE (deck+analysis hash), EM (geometry+freq-sweep hash), and CFD (mesh+BC hash) so re-runs of unchanged studies are O(load). Never serve a stale result: any input-hash mismatch is a miss. Respect the resource_governor 20MB/studies cap.
acceptance: unchanged FEA study reload is a cache HIT with byte-identical result and >5x wall-clock speedup
any mesh/BC/material/deck/freq input change is a MISS (no stale results ever)
SPICE + EM + CFD result caches round-trip and invalidate on input-hash change
studies stay under the contract 20MB cap; governor low-memory disables the cache honestly
existing sim accuracy gates unchanged

nodes.end_condition: Repeated identical sim studies load from cache with cited speedup; every input change invalidates correctly.

nodes.name: F2: Nested-tree (file-tree) profiler + scoped drill-down

inputs.request: Add a nested call-tree report to core/prof: aggregate the existing folded stacks into a hierarchical tree (parent->children with self/total samples + %), and give phases.cpp a nested phase-tree report (study->phase->subphase) instead of flat lists. Emit as compact nested JSON so an agent reads the ROOT + hot children first and drills down by path (context-frugal, like a file tree) rather than ingesting the whole flat profile. Expose via the MCP engine_profile surface with a `path` selector for scoped subtree reads and a depth cap. Keep the existing folded/speedscope exports intact.
acceptance: build_tree produces a correct parent/child self+total sample tree from a known folded-stack fixture
phases report is nested study->phase->subphase with wall-clock rollups
MCP profile read returns ROOT + top-N children within a token budget and supports path-scoped drill-down + depth cap
folded + speedscope exports still byte-match the pre-change format

nodes.end_condition: Profiler emits a nested tree an agent can drill down by path without ingesting the whole trace.

nodes.name: F3: Dynamic resource governance (no OOM, no self-throttle) + shared thread pool

inputs.request: Upgrade core/util/resource_governor from binary admit to a dynamic governor: track live RSS + available memory and grade heavy ops (mesh/FEA/CFD/EM/ECAD-route) with an adaptive concurrency + thread budget that fills available CPU/RAM WITHOUT crossing the OOM headroom (avoid throttling when resources are free, avoid OOM when they are not). Add a small shared work-queue/thread-pool primitive (bounded by the governor) so solvers stop each spawning ad-hoc OMP regions that oversubscribe. Wire the pool + governor into the LBM, FEA assembly, and ECAD autoroute hot paths. Every limit decision must be observable (report) and env-overridable.
acceptance: under a synthetic low-memory cap the governor reduces concurrency and NEVER exceeds the headroom (no OOM)
with ample memory the governor uses ~all allotted cores (no artificial throttle)
thread pool caps total worker threads to the governed budget (no oversubscription across nested solves)
every admission/thread decision is in the governor report; env overrides honored
existing governor tests still pass

nodes.end_condition: Heavy ops scale to available resources without OOM and without self-throttling; threads are pooled under one budget.

nodes.name: F4: Flight-computer + battery-charger parts pack (symbols/footprints/eng/sim params)

inputs.request: Add real electronics parts to the clean-room ECAD starter library so both benchmark boards build end-to-end from the Parts Library. Flight computer: an MCU (STM32F4-class QFP), 6-axis IMU (accel+gyro, I2C/SPI), barometer (I2C), magnetometer (I2C), a GNSS/GPS module (UART), a buck or LDO 3V3 rail, decoupling/passives, crystal, SWD header, USB. Battery charger: a Li-ion charger controller topology (linear + switching option), power MOSFETs, current-sense resistor, low-voltage-disconnect comparator/load-switch, protection (reverse, OVP/UVP), thermistor, inductor, bulk caps. Each part: pin-correct symbol + footprint (pins subset of pads), eng metadata (supply rails/currents for boardphys + power_budget), and SPICE model refs/params where a device is simulated. Keep clean-room (no vendor netlists copied); make each resolvable via ecad_find_part/part_search.
acceptance: ecad_find_part returns >=1 pin-correct hit for imu, barometer, magnetometer, gps, charger_controller, power_mosfet, current_sense, load_switch
every new symbol's pin numbers are a subset of its footprint pads
each powered part carries eng supply-rail metadata consumed by power_budget
a minimal flight-computer AND a minimal charger schematic place + ERC-clean using only starter/pack parts

nodes.end_condition: Both benchmark boards can be built from the Parts Library with pin-correct, sim-ready parts.

nodes.name: E1: Connectivity-aware deterministic auto-placement

inputs.request: Upgrade op_pcb_autoplace beyond the fixed grid into a deterministic connectivity-aware placer: cluster components by net degree, seat decoupling caps adjacent to their IC power pins, keep connectors on the board edge, respect courtyards (no overlap), and honor placement hints/locks. Deterministic (seeded) so the same netlist yields the same layout. This is the placement half of 'preliminary board from schematic'.
acceptance: decoupling caps land within a small radius of their IC power pin
no courtyard overlaps after placement (DRC courtyard clean)
connectors placed on a board edge
placement is deterministic for a fixed netlist+seed
total ratsnest length strictly shorter than the old grid placement on a >=15-component board

nodes.end_condition: Placement is connectivity-aware, overlap-free, deterministic, and shortens ratsnest vs grid.

nodes.name: E2: Curved/arc + teardrop + impedance-driven trace optimization

inputs.request: Add a post-route trace-optimization pass over the existing Lee/A* segment output: (a) corner rounding — replace 90-degree corners with arc tracks (schema kind=arc already supported; fab tessellates ~5deg) to reduce discontinuity/impedance; (b) teardrops at pad/via junctions; (c) impedance-driven width adjustment — using IPC-2141 impedance.cpp + stackup inverse, widen/narrow nets tagged with a target Z0 to hit it within tolerance; (d) DRC-safe: every transformation re-checks clearance and reverts locally on violation. Deterministic and idempotent.
acceptance: 90-degree corners become arcs; routed board stays DRC-clean
teardrops added at pad/via transitions without clearance violations
a net tagged target Z0=50ohm is width-adjusted to within tolerance per ecad_check_impedance
pass is deterministic + idempotent (second run is a no-op)
fab export (gerber) round-trips the arc tracks

nodes.end_condition: Rigid segment routes become smooth arc/teardrop/impedance-tuned traces, DRC-clean and deterministic.

nodes.name: E3: PCB antenna design helpers + EM solver bridge

inputs.request: Add parametric PCB antenna design helpers: rectangular patch, quarter-wave monopole, meandered inverted-F (PIFA/IFA for 2.4GHz), and CPW/microstrip feed calculators (dimensions from target frequency + substrate epsilon_r/height using standard closed-form design equations, cross-checked against the existing IPC-2141/CPWG impedance code for the feed). Generate the antenna as real PCB copper geometry (traces/zones) on the board, and bridge to the EM suite: build the analytic/FDFD model and, when openEMS is present, the full-wave model, returning resonant frequency + return-loss/S11 estimate. Honest skip (design geometry + analytic estimate only) when openEMS is absent — never fabricate a full-wave result.
acceptance: patch/monopole/IFA dimension calc matches textbook design equations within a few %
generated antenna is real DRC-checkable board copper
feed impedance cross-checks the IPC-2141/CPWG code
EM bridge returns an analytic resonance estimate always, and a full-wave S11 when openEMS present (honest skip otherwise)

nodes.end_condition: Agents can design a PCB antenna parametrically, place it as real copper, and evaluate it via the EM suite (honest under missing openEMS).

nodes.name: E4: Deterministic schematic->preliminary-PCB + AI board-design workflow tools

inputs.request: Wire the full board-design workflow the agent follows: (1) schematic-first — capture/generate schematic from a request; (2) simulate — SPICE the schematic until it exhibits target behavior (gate); (3) preliminary board — ONE deterministic tool that takes the simulated schematic and emits a placed + pre-routed board (uses E1 placement + existing autoroute + E2 trace-opt) to save layout time; (4) board-level checks — impedance/DRC/DFM/PDN/thermal/vibe/EM; (5) firmware. Add/repair the MCP tool surface so an agent has a correct, discoverable tool for each step (a board_from_schematic one-call, plus the guidance in cad_guide). Keep every stage honest and re-runnable.
acceptance: board_from_schematic turns a simulated schematic into a placed+pre-routed board in one call, DRC-clean or with named residual violations
the schematic->simulate->layout->check->firmware tool path is complete and discoverable (each step has a tool)
the preliminary board reuses E1/E2 (no duplicate placer/router)
re-running board_from_schematic on an unchanged schematic is deterministic

nodes.end_condition: An agent can go schematic->simulate->preliminary PCB->checks->firmware with a correct tool at each step.

nodes.name: S1: CFD/aero/kinematic -> sensor-model -> firmware-emulation bridge + real sensor models

inputs.request: Build the bridge that feeds SIMULATED REALITY into the emulated MCU. Add physics-accurate sensor models that convert sim time-series into aicad.fwscenario/1 tracks: 6-axis IMU (accel+gyro from a kinematic/rigid-body trajectory incl. gravity + body rates), barometer (pressure/altitude from an atmosphere model driven by a flight-profile or CFD field), magnetometer (heading), GNSS (position/velocity fix), pitot/airspeed (from CFD or flight profile). Extend scenario.py to support TIME-VARYING i2c_register streams (register bytes as a function of t) so a moving sensor value plays back over emulation; encode each model to its part's real register map (ties to F4 parts). Provide a bridge tool: given a motion/CFD/aero sim result (or an analytic flight profile) + a board's sensors, generate the fwscenario that plays that reality into fw_sim_run. Honest skip when Renode absent (fwscenario needs Renode) with a clear reason; keep QEMU semihosting path working for UART-only checks.
acceptance: IMU model reproduces known accel/gyro for a canned trajectory (free-fall ~0g, static ~1g down, spin -> gyro rate) within tolerance
barometer model maps a known altitude profile to correct pressures
scenario.py plays a time-varying i2c_register stream that changes the value the firmware reads over time (verified via a trace assertion)
the bridge turns a motion/flight-profile sim into a valid fwscenario consumed by fw_sim_run (Renode present) or honest-skips (absent) with reason

nodes.end_condition: A CFD/kinematic/flight-profile sim can drive realistic IMU/baro/mag/GPS readings into the emulated firmware.

nodes.name: S2: Opportunistic GPU/CUDA + parallelization expansion (scoped by D3)

inputs.request: Per decision D3, extend GPU/parallel acceleration where it is a clear, safe win beyond the existing CUDA LBM: candidate targets = FEA global assembly + sparse SpMV/solve (batched), EM FDFD eigensolve, and batched SPICE parameter sweeps (Monte-Carlo / .step) which are embarrassingly parallel across the shared thread pool (F3). Every GPU path MUST have a validated CPU fallback and be gated (CHUDWARE_WITH_CUDA / runtime device probe) — never a hard dependency. Cross-check GPU results against the CPU path within accuracy tolerance. Use the F3 governor/thread-pool so parallel sweeps do not oversubscribe or OOM.
acceptance: each new GPU path matches its CPU reference within accuracy tolerance
each GPU path falls back cleanly with no CUDA device / CHUDWARE_WITH_CUDA off
batched SPICE sweep parallelizes across the F3 pool with a cited speedup and no oversubscription
no new hard GPU dependency in the default build

nodes.end_condition: Selected solvers gain governed GPU/parallel speedups with validated CPU fallbacks (scope per D3).

nodes.name: B1: Flight-computer E2E benchmark

inputs.request: Author scripts/bench_flight_computer.py exercising the WHOLE suite: pull MCU/IMU/baro/mag/GPS/regulator from the Parts Library (providers priced when credentialed, honest-skip otherwise) -> generate + SPICE-simulate the power/sensor front-end schematic -> board_from_schematic deterministic preliminary PCB -> E2 trace-opt + antenna (GNSS/2.4GHz) -> render -> board-level checks (impedance, DRC/DFM, PDN, ECAD->thermal, ECAD->vibe) -> firmware project + build -> fw_sim_run driven by S1 sensor bridge feeding IMU/baro readings derived from a kinematic/aero flight-profile sim -> fw_verify_board -> power_budget -> report. Governed (resource_governor), solve-state-cached (F1), and profiled (F2 nested tree). Every stage asserts a concrete pass/fail; backends absent => honest SKIP markers, never fabricated success.

board is DRC-clean (or residuals named), impedance/PDN/thermal/vibe checks return numeric verdicts

nodes.name: B2: Battery charger/controller E2E benchmark (LVD + charge optimization + safety)

inputs.request: Author scripts/bench_battery_charger.py: design a Li-ion battery charger/controller with a low-voltage disconnect, charge-profile optimization (CC/CV stages, taper termination), and safety heuristics (over-voltage/under-voltage/over-current/over-temperature cutoffs, reverse-polarity protection, thermal foldback). Pull charger controller/MOSFET/current-sense/load-switch/thermistor from the Parts Library -> SPICE-simulate the analog charge/discharge behavior across load and battery-state, verifying CC->CV transition, taper-off termination, and that each safety cutoff actually trips at its threshold; LVD disconnects the load at the set voltage -> board_from_schematic PCB with adequate power-trace widths (impedance/ampacity) + ECAD->thermal on the pass device -> firmware charge state-machine (states: precharge/CC/CV/done/fault) with the safety cutoffs, emulated and asserted (fault entry on injected over-temp/over-voltage) -> power_budget/report. Governed, cached, profiled. Honest SKIP where backends absent.
acceptance: SPICE shows a correct CC->CV charge curve with taper termination and an LVD that disconnects at the set threshold
each safety cutoff (OVP/UVP/OCP/OTP) trips at its threshold in simulation
PCB power traces meet width/ampacity + thermal on the pass device
firmware charge state-machine reaches DONE on a full charge and enters FAULT on injected over-temp/over-voltage via the sensor bridge
wired into scripts/gate.sh as an env-gated stage; honest skips where backends absent

nodes.end_condition: The charger is designed, simulated (charge profile + safety trips + LVD), laid out, and firmware-emulated with asserted safety behavior.

This is the 'new testing protocols' deliverable — it must cover the entire ECAD suite and its integrations with the simulation suite and the 3D/physical-modeling section (housing integration via ecad->3d/boardphys).
acceptance: harness runs both benchmarks + the ECAD/sim/3D integration checks under one governed, cached, profiled protocol
single consolidated report with per-stage verdicts + nested profile
gate.sh wires it env-gated (skip-clean on unprovisioned boxes)

nodes.end_condition: One governed/cached/profiled protocol covers the whole ECAD+sim+3D range with a consolidated verdict.
